mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-origin document: notarize at a Taiwan district court notary office, verify through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), and verify through the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); this cross-strait path replaces both Apostille and consular legalization. For any document from a Hague Apostille Convention member state, the competent authority of that state must issue an Apostille; for a non-member state, the PRC Embassy or Consulate performs consular legalization. The Apostille and consular legalization paths are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, every UBO, legal representative, director, supervisor, senior manager, and authorized signatory of the WFOE and its upstream parent must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, the PRC PBOC and state security watch lists, the Ministry of Public Security prohibition list, and Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission designated persons list. Screening must cover negative news, PEP status, politically exposed family members, source of wealth, source of funds, politically connected entity risks, and cross-border frozen asset indicators. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and any beneficial owner connected to high-risk jurisdictions, with results recorded in the AML/CFT file and refreshed quarterly for at least three years after incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration and Administration System operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (online name clearance portal at name.samr.gov.cn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory names must be in Simplified Chinese characters. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) administrative division at province, city, or county level; (2) a distinctive trade name; (3) an industry description matching the permitted business scope; and (4) the legal form marker 'Limited Liability Company'. A foreign investor's name may be transliterated into Pinyin as the trade name; an English duplicate name is permitted only as a non-statutory secondary name and must be identical in meaning to the Chinese name. No mixed-script names and no abbreviations are allowed in the official Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant should first read the electronic rejection reason and may file a corrected name application immediately. To contest the rejection, file an administrative reconsideration application with the deciding SAMR authority or its superior within 15 working days of the electronic notice. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within 6 months. The applicant must preserve the name application number, the rejection notice, the trade name evidence, and any prior-use or consent documents. If rejection is based on confusing similarity, a consent letter from the prior company may cure the defect. A reserved name may be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing before the initial reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a fast-fashion e-commerce WFOE, a virtual office is rejected by local tax authorities for VAT and enterprise income tax registration, invoice quota approval, and export tax rebate procedures, and by commercial banks for RMB and foreign-exchange account opening. SAMR may accept a cluster registration address only in designated free trade zones or business incubators, but tax and bank acceptance remains conditional on actual management substance, lease records, staff presence, and operational evidence. A pure commercial mailbox is not acceptable as a statutory registered address for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 85% if a virtual or mailbox address is used, and 15-25% if a dedicated physical office with a proper lease is maintained. Checklist of inspection triggers: no utility bills under the company name; use of a residential address; no employees at the registered site; e-commerce inventory stored at a different unregistered warehouse; tax filings showing zero income despite active online sales; landlord not holding title to the property; and discrepancies between the SAMR-registered address, bank settlement account address, and customs registration. Maintain lease contracts, landlord property certificates, utility invoices, attendance records, inventory logs, e-commerce platform backend records, bank reconciliation statements, import and export declarations, board minutes, and tax returns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: People's Republic of China Company Law (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4-10, 23-47, 53-58, 75, 180, 182-184, 232; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 12, 26, 34; Administrative Regulations on Registration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746), Articles 2, 5, 8, 15-18; Interim Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting; and cross-strait investment rules applicable to Taiwan investors, including the Provisions on Encouragement of Investment by Taiwanese Compatriots. The investor is treated as a Taiwan-source foreign investor for the PRC WFOE formation, subject to non-restricted treatment for e-commerce apparel retail under the current Foreign Investment Negative List.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Administration for Market Regulation at the intended registered office in mainland China, together with the local Department of Commerce for Taiwan investor filing and a SAFE-designated bank for foreign exchange registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company / Business License Application, filed through the local SAMR one-stop enterprise registration system, together with the Foreign Investment Information Report and the Taiwan Compatriot Investment Filing Form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a PRC WFOE engaged in electronic retail of fast-fashion apparel and footwear under ISIC 4791. The sole Taiwan shareholder must set a registered capital amount in the Articles of Association that is reasonably suited to the business scale. Under the 2024 PRC Company Law, the registered capital must be fully subscribed and paid in within the statutory maximum contribution period, generally five years from establishment, unless a shorter period is adopted in the Articles. No blocked escrow account is mandated; however, the subscribed capital must be remitted from outside mainland China into a designated capital contribution account at a Chinese bank with SAFE foreign-exchange qualification, and the actual paid-in capital must be subsequently reported in the SAFE FDI information system and the SAMR annual report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD, A Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company, Adopted on [Date] by the Sole Shareholder and First Board/Executive Director of CN WFOE LTD (the "Company") pursuant to the PRC Company Law (2023 Revision), the PRC Foreign Investment Law, and the Articles of Association of the Company. WHEREAS the Company is to be established as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company in the People's Republic of China, with a single shareholder resident in Taiwan; and WHEREAS the sole shareholder has subscribed in full to the registered capital and the authorized officers shall take all steps necessary to complete formation. NOW THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. Share Capital Subscription and Payment. RESOLVED, that the total registered capital of the Company be [Amount in RMB] Yuan, divided into [Number] units of contributed capital, and that the sole shareholder subscribes to all such units. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscribed capital be paid into a temporary capital contribution account opened at [Bank Name] in the Company's name no later than [Date], and that the Executive Director shall procure a capital verification report if required by the local Administration for Market Regulation or the applicable bank. 2. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered address and principal place of business of the Company be [Full Address], that the office lease and ownership certificate attached to the minutes are genuine and effective, and that the registered address shall be used for all statutory notices. 3. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Executive Director, [Name] be appointed Supervisor, and [Name] be appointed General Manager and legal representative. The General Manager is authorized to conduct day-to-day affairs, conclude contracts, open bank accounts, hire employees, and delegate authority to subordinate managers as necessary. 4. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the General Manager and the financial controller jointly authorize the opening of one or more bank accounts with [Bank], and that banking instructions shall be effective when signed by two designated signatories or as the bank's mandate may require. 5. Certification and Implementation. RESOLVED, that the legal representative and external counsel are irrevocably authorized to execute and file all instrumentalities, including foreign investment information reports, Taiwan investor filing, tax registration, and any application before government agencies, and to affix the Company seal. Any director or the Executive Director may waive notice of any further meeting, and such meeting may be held by telephone or video conference. ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY on [Date] at [Place].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Name Pre-Registration and Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) online enterprise registration portal / National Enterprise Registration Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for pre-approval of the proposed Chinese and English company name and for the business scope of electronic retail of fast-fashion apparel and footwear. The applicant must select the entity type 'Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (Limited Liability)' and map the intended business scope to the official SAMR business scope classification corresponding to ISIC 4791. Confirm that the Taiwan investor is entering a permitted sector outside the Foreign Investment Negative List and that the name contains no prohibited, misleading, reserved, or trademark-conflicting characters. The enterprise name should generally follow the format: Administrative Region + Trade Name + Industry Characteristics + Company Limited. Retain the approved name registration notice for use in subsequent incorporation filings.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name and English name
Taiwan investor identification or parent company certificate
Proposed business scope and ISIC mapping
Projected registered capital and contribution period
Authorized agent letter of appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or conflict with an existing enterprise, revise and re-file a new name application through the same portal. If the business scope is flagged as restricted or subject to special pre-approval, obtain a written explanation from the SAMR and, if necessary, redraft the scope or seek sector-regulator pre-approval before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taiwan Investor Filing and Cross-Strait Investment Recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Department of Commerce (MOFCOM Taiwan-Hong Kong-Macao Investment Filing window) in coordination with the SAMR one-stop Foreign Investment Information Report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Taiwan-source investor must complete the Taiwan Compatriot Investment filing or applicable prior recordal through the local commerce authority for a permitted-sector investment. The filing confirms the investor's identity, source of funds, investment ratio, registered capital amount, and operating scope. Because the WFOE will conduct only e-commerce retail of apparel, which is not on the Negative List, the procedure is generally a filing rather than a substantive approval. Submit the Foreign Investment Information Report together with the Taiwan investor filing form, and ensure that the investor's name in Chinese and in the Taiwanese corporate register matches the notarized and authenticated documents. The local commerce department will issue a filing receipt or confirmation that must accompany the final enterprise registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized and cross-strait authenticated Taiwan investor identity or corporate registration certificate
Bank reference and source-of-funds statement
Business plan for the fast-fashion apparel e-commerce operation
Proposed registered capital and capital contribution schedule
Completed Taiwan Compatriot Investment Filing Form and Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Taiwan investment filing is suspended for source-of-funds or identity verification, submit supplementary notarized bank statements, audited financials, and certified copies of the Taiwanese parent entity's registration records. If the filing is rejected on the basis of restricted Negative List activity, restructure the scope to remove the prohibited item or apply for a formal MOFCOM review with a reasoned legal memorandum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Articles of Association and Application for Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) enterprise registration window or the official one-stop online registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name pre-approval and the Taiwan investment filing, submit the duly executed Articles of Association, the first board/shareholder resolution, the legal representative appointment letter, the supervisor and general manager identity documents, and the office lease with ownership certificate or lease-filing receipt. The business scope must expressly include online retail of clothing, footwear and apparel accessories. The SAMR will conduct a formal completeness review, verify compliance with the PRC Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law, and issue the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Business License with the Unified Social Credit Code. The registered address must be a lawfully rentable commercial premises; if the local government requires a separate building-use certificate, that certificate must be attached. The license issuance completes the statutory incorporation and creates the legal personality of the WFOE.
required_dossiers: Signed enterprise establishment registration application form
Articles of Association subscribed by the Taiwan investor
First board/shareholder resolution and officer appointment documents
Enterprise name pre-approval notice
Office lease contract and property ownership certificate or lease-filing proof
Identity documents of director, supervisor, general manager and legal representative
Taiwan investor filing receipt and Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR issues an amendment notice, correct the identified provisions, such as capital contribution timing, business scope, or registered address documentation, and resubmit within the statutory correction period. If the registered address is deemed non-compliant because of residential-use restrictions, replace the lease with a certified commercial-use property and file the revised lease-filing receipt; the application will then resume from the point of interruption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-License Establishment: Seals, Tax and Social Insurance Registration, and SAFE Foreign Exchange Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (for seal engraving), State Taxation Administration / local tax bureau, social insurance and housing fund offices, and a SAFE-designated foreign exchange bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the Business License, engrave the company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal through a public-security-registered engraving service. Register the WFOE with the local tax authority for income tax, value-added tax, and invoice issuance within the statutory post-registration period, and complete social insurance and housing fund enrollment for employees. Open a basic deposit account and a foreign-exchange capital contribution account at a bank authorized by SAFE, complete the SAFE foreign-invested enterprise registration through the banks, and remit the Taiwan investor's capital contribution from abroad into the capital contribution account. Convert the foreign currency into RMB as needed and report the actual paid-in capital in the SAMR annual report and the SAFE FDI information system. If the company will directly import or export goods, also complete customs registration for cross-border e-commerce.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Legal representative and company seal specimens
Seal engraving approval from the Public Security Bureau
Articles of Association and Taiwan investor filing receipt
Bank account opening application and SAFE registration forms
Tax registration form and office lease certificate
Taiwan investor remittance instruction and source-of-funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, file a correction with the tax service hall and pay any administrative warning fee. If SAFE rejects the FDI registration because of mismatched investor names, cure the defect by submitting certifying notarized Chinese/English name statements and the authenticated Taiwan investor authorization to the bank. If the first bank declines the capital account opening, apply to a second SAFE-designated bank and resubmit the electronic Business License and investor filing confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Commerce Accessibility and Digital Compliance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) through the local Communications Administration for ICP filing, and the local SAMR for E-Commerce Law compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the WFOE operates a public-facing website, app, or miniprogram for fast-fashion apparel retail, complete the ICP filing for non-commercial internet information services. For a pure self-operated online store selling the company's own apparel and footwear, a full value-added telecommunications license is not generally mandatory; however, if the operation becomes a third-party marketplace or sells information services, an online data processing and transaction processing license may be required. Publish the business license information, privacy policy, terms of sale, returns and refund policy, and customer service contact in compliance with the PRC E-Commerce Law and consumer-protection rules. Maintain transaction records, anti-money-laundering procedures, and secure payment data handling for the target payment rails such as BNPL and payment service providers.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Legal representative and website operator identity documents
Domain name or app/miniprogram registration certificate
Hosting or cloud service agreement
Internet information services filing form and information security management measures
E-commerce compliance policies and payment data security policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MIIT rejects the ICP filing, correct the subject details, website domain ownership, or service provider information and resubmit. If the filing is suspended because the website is not yet accessible, use the hosting provider's filing-acceptance gateway to complete the process. If the local Communications Administration determines that licensed value-added telecom services apply, either restructure the platform to operate strictly as a self-operated retailer or apply for the appropriate telecommunications business license before accepting online orders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 electronic retail of fast-fashion apparel and footwear does not involve manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operations. The applicable regulators for general online retail are the SAMR and the State Taxation Administration; if the WFOE operates its own website, the MIIT/local Communications Administration ICP filing requirement applies as an administrative registration rather than an industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial production license, hazardous chemical operating permit, food/drug permit, or manufacturing license is required for this fast-fashion apparel e-commerce retail scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) permitting is not triggered by an office-based online retail activity. Environmental review would only be triggered if the WFOE later establishes an apparel factory, dyeing/printing plant, or large logistics warehouse.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no Full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, or exemption declaration is required for pure electronic retail. If a future warehouse or fulfillment depot over the local threshold is established, an environmental impact registration or filing under the PRC Environmental Impact Assessment Law and the MEE classification catalogue may become mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there is no fixed industrial discharge point, VOC emission source, or hazardous-waste generation stream from the e-commerce activity. General office solid waste must be handled through municipal sanitation. Any future warehouse or logistics operation must comply with applicable ambient air, noise, and solid/hazardous waste standards under GB 16297, GB 12348, and GB 18599 and must obtain the necessary waste-management filings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no manufacturing or factory premises are involved, so no Civil Defense fire permit or structural load inspection is required. The leased office must nonetheless comply with the PRC Fire Protection Law; the landlord must hold a valid building fire-safety inspection certificate for the premises, and the WFOE should implement workplace fire evacuation procedures, emergency lighting, and occupational safety measures for its office and retail support staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), with the taxpayer's provincial e-Tax Bureau electronic portal accessible from the STA official website at www.chinatax.gov.cn. If a separate Taiwan taxable presence is established, the competent authority for that market is the Taxation Administration of the Ministry of Finance, Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The China-incorporated WFOE obtains its 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the local Administration for Market Regulation in the province of incorporation; the USCC is the sole taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT identification number. The registration record is automatically transmitted to the STA under the integrated one-stop tax registration process, and no separate tax registration certificate is issued. The WFOE must complete post-registration formalities in the e-Tax Bureau within 30 calendar days, including bank account filing, accounting method reporting and VAT taxpayer status confirmation. A foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese establishment does not use the USCC route; its China-source income is reported through a withholding registration using the non-resident entity's identification data and the payer's tax profile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise for Enterprise Income Tax and is therefore taxed at entity level on worldwide income; for indirect tax purposes it is a VAT taxpayer, initially classified as either a small-scale taxpayer or a general VAT taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for pass-through treatment; a PRC limited liability WFOE cannot elect transparent status. A small-scale VAT taxpayer may elect once to become a general VAT taxpayer if it satisfies the prescribed accounting and filing conditions. China does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election for this entity type.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax), with a zero-rated export regime for qualifying outbound goods; Taiwan Business Tax will apply to the WFOE only if a separate Taiwan taxable presence is established or a Taiwan importer triggers the Taiwan tax obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Every China-incorporated company must complete tax registration within 30 days after incorporation; there is no turnover exemption from registration. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 within any consecutive 12-month period; below that threshold the WFOE may remain a small-scale taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates invoice issuance through the STA Full Digital Electronic Invoice service platform and tax-controlled invoice equipment for general taxpayers. Invoice data is transmitted electronically to the STA for near real-time validation and cross-matching; each invoice carries a tax authority verification code and QR code for anti-fraud checks. Certified API integrations with approved accounting or enterprise resource planning systems are available for large-scale issuers, but China does not operate a pre-clearance fiscal stamping model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported fast-fashion apparel sold by the WFOE to Taiwan or other foreign customers qualifies for VAT zero-rating when the goods are physically exported from China and cleared by China Customs in the name of the exporting WFOE. The WFOE must be a general VAT taxpayer to claim the input VAT refund; small-scale taxpayers receive simplified export exemption rather than a zero-rated refund.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export goods declaration) cleared by China Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export shipment
Export sales contract or purchase order
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA cross-checks export tax refund claims against customs export declarations, transport documentation, sales contracts and foreign-exchange collection records. If the zero-rating cannot be substantiated, the refund is reversed and late-payment interest is charged. Under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection, deliberate underpayment or false claims may result in a fine of 50% to five times the tax involved; fraudulent export refund claims may constitute the criminal offence of fraudulent export tax refund under the Criminal Law, with imprisonment and monetary penalties.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% flat profit-seeking enterprise (corporate) income tax rate under Article 5, Income Tax Act.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for fast-fashion e-commerce. Standard deductions apply. Retained earnings surtax of 5% on undistributed profits under Article 66-9. R&D and investment tax credits may offset up to 30% of corporate income tax, but only for approved innovative sectors; not generally available to pure e-commerce importers. Alternative Minimum Tax at 12% applies to basic income exceeding TWD 6.7 million, but is rarely triggered by apparel e-commerce without securities gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 10) filed via the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing Portal (e-tax, https://tax.nat.gov.tw). Annual filing includes the Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Disclosure Schedule (Schedule B-3).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance payments of estimated tax (June 30 and September 30) are required but not final.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year enterprises, final annual return due 31 May of the following year. For fiscal-year enterprises, within five months after fiscal year-end (e.g., a 30 June year-end requires filing by 30 November).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenues: e-commerce sales of fast-fashion apparel, footwear and related logistics income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan resident WFOE reports worldwide gross sales. Sales to offshore customers are fully taxable. For non-resident branch filers, report only Taiwan-source sales and apportion expenses under the branch profit calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: inventory costs, inbound freight and customs, payment-processing gateway fees and direct packing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All direct costs must be supported by invoices and inventory records. Cross-border purchases from affiliated suppliers must reflect an arm's length purchase price; otherwise adjust in the TP report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: platform commissions, digital advertising, warehouse lease, employee payroll, shipping labels, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in earning the taxable income are deductible. Intercompany marketing fees paid to a foreign affiliate must pass the benefit, arm's length and withholding tests; overseas service fees are subject to 20% WHT unless treaty-reduced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating revenue and expenses: interest income, FX gains/losses, recoveries and other income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Taiwan-source interest and dividend income. Foreign taxes paid on non-Taiwan sources may be claimed as foreign tax credits using the Foreign Tax Credit Computation Schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (or loss) after carryforwards: deduct available loss carried forward (10-year term) and any statutory exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax losses may offset taxable income if the WFOE maintains proper books and records under IFRS. For non-resident enterprises without a fixed place, only income effectively connected with a Taiwan PE is netted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax at 20%: computed tax before advance payments, credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident enterprises are taxed per country; foreign branch profits are taxable in Taiwan with FTC. Non-residents with a Taiwan PE are taxed at the same 20% rate on income attributable to the PE; distributions to head office are subject to 20% branch profit remittance tax unless exempted by treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of tax already paid abroad subject to FTC, and prepaid tax, withholding tax and provisional advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign income taxes paid, but FTC cannot exceed the Taiwan tax attributable to the foreign-source income. Submit the FTC computation schedule with the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: additional tax of 3% per month (or part), maximum 30% of assessed tax; fixed penalty NT$1,500 if no tax due. Late payment: surcharge of 1% per every two days, capped at 15%; daily interest at the Central Bank one-year postal savings deposit rate plus 1% is assessed on unpaid amounts. Falsification or concealment invokes Article 110 penalties of 2 to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders without a fixed business establishment in Taiwan (Articles 88 and 89, Income Tax Act). For resident corporate shareholders, dividend income is included in taxable income with no additional WHT; a 5% retained earnings surtax is imposed on the Taiwan distributing company on undistributed surplus.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend WHT under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement (or an OECD DTA), the foreign parent must obtain a Resident Tax Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority (for mainland China, the State Taxation Administration) and provide it to the Taiwan paying company before the dividend declaration. The Taiwan payer then files a reduced-withholding application with the National Taxation Bureau; the official reduced rates under the Cross-Strait Agreement are 5% (when the beneficial owner holds directly at least 25% of the equity capital and meets certain investment amount requirements, or 10% in other cases). Substantial economic substance in the residence country must be demonstrated via payroll, premises and commercial activity. Without a TRC and proof of beneficial ownership, the payer must withhold at the 21% statutory rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Taiwan WHT on payments to non-residents: royalties for industrial/commercial/scientific equipment or IP licensing — 20% (gross); interest on non-financial loans — 20% (gross); interest on financial institution deposits — 15% (gross). Treaty/Cross-Strait reductions: interest generally 10% (7% for financial institutions under the Cross-Strait Arrangement); royalties generally 10% (7% for equipment rentals) if the beneficial owner meets the treaty test. Failure to withhold and deposit the WHT within 10 days after the payment triggers a penalty of up to 1.5 times the unwithheld tax under Article 114 of the Income Tax Act.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Taiwan WFOE must prepare a Local File (transfer pricing report) when aggregate controlled (related-party) transactions exceed TWD 60 million in the fiscal year; a Master File is required when the ultimate parent's global consolidated revenue exceeds TWD 300 million and the Taiwan entity engages in cross-border related-party transactions. The Related-Party Transactions Disclosure (Schedule B-3) must be filed with the annual CIT return even if below the documentation threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no standalone ESR but applies substance-over-form and GAAR provisions. To claim treaty benefits, the WFOE must have genuine operating substance: business premises, management and board decisions in Taiwan, employees, and a real commercial function in the e-commerce retail chain. A shell company with no substantial activities (no warehouse, no marketing team, no risk-bearing capacity) will have its intercompany arrangements disregarded; income will be recomputed under the arm's length principle; and dividends or royalties may be recharacterized as taxable distributions to the foreign shareholder, triggering 21% WHT and potential penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Income Tax Act Article 110, Tax Collection Act Article 41)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting e-commerce sales through offshore platforms, concealment of PayPal/BNPL settlement deposits, use of nominee owner bank or payment accounts, and failure to file the annual CIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of two to three times the evaded tax (determined by the audit bureau); where willful tax evasion is proven, the responsible person may be criminally fined and imprisoned for up to seven years under the Tax Collection Act; unpaid tax plus daily interest is collected through compulsory enforcement and travel bans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false tax returns are personally liable for restitution of the evaded tax, statutory fines, and criminal penalties; legal representatives may be prohibited from leaving Taiwan and their personal properties can be seized for unpaid taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the WFOE with nominal capital, no employees, no premises, and routing 80–100% of the e-commerce service income to a mainland China-related party through inflated management fees or intercompany royalties, while the WFOE bears no risk and performs no development functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taiwan tax authority may disregard the WFOE's legal personality under Article 12-1 (GAAR), recharacterize the revenue as attributable to the foreign shareholder, impose transfer pricing adjustment and re-characterize a deemed dividend, and assess a 21% WHT plus interest and penalties of 2–3 times the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as 'responsible persons' face joint personal liability for the re-assessed tax and penalties; they can be subject to a travel ban, a hold-in-depth hearing, and, under extreme fraudulent circumstances, criminal fraud charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Paperwork Failure and Advanced Pricing Agreement Absence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and submit the TP Local File/Master File when the TWD 60 million related-party transaction threshold is exceeded; providing incomplete or false comparability analyses; ignoring arm's length documentation for the intercompany purchase of apparel from a mainland factory affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority applies the best-method adjustment, disallows the intercompany expenses, and imputes the difference to taxable income; the taxpayer is then subject to an additional tax of 20% plus a penalty of up to 2 times the difference under Article 110; repeated non-compliance can lead to an audit penalty and publication of the taxpayer's name.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/shareholders who approve disregard of TP rules may be personally liable for the resulting underpaid taxes, and may lose their entitlement to administrative remedies; any attempt to falsely certify the transfer pricing report constitutes perjury in tax procedure and can trigger criminal consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance on Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to the mainland China parent or royalties/interest to an offshore affiliate without collecting the statutory WHT (21% for dividends, 20% for royalties/interest) and without applying the Cross-Strait/treaty reduction via an approved TRC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 114 imposes a penalty of up to 1.5 times the unwithheld amount, plus the tax itself; if the company fails to withhold, the foreign payee remains liable for the tax together with a late-filing surcharge; the tax authority can stop the distribution by freezing the company's bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who knowingly cause the non-withholding are jointly liable with the company for the unpaid WHT and penalties; they may be held personally responsible in insolvency proceedings and face criminal sanctions under the Tax Collection Act.
